tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

CHANGE_REQUEST.md
# One-Slide Pitch — Maintenance Handbook Assistant

**Audience:** the business owner who runs maintenance operations (non-technical).
**Source of truth:** `specs/MASTER_SPEC.md`, `docs/INTENT_BRIEF.md`, `index/report.json`, and a live run of the working assistant on 2026-11-01.
**Editable slide:** `docs/ONE_SLIDE_PITCH.pptx` (one slide, 90-second talk track in the speaker notes).
**Case note:** the demo uses the public FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician General Handbook as a stand-in for the client's own documents.

---

## The slide

**Title:** Ask a maintenance question in plain English. Get a cited answer from every chapter that matters.

| The problem today | What we built | What you see |
|---|---|---|
| Technicians ask questions that touch several chapters. A single search finds one piece and misses the rest. | A chat assistant that has read all 14 handbook chapters (633 pages). | A plain-English answer, with each statement tagged to its chapter, section and page. |

**Live example (real output, not a mock):**
> *"How do I recognize corrosion on aluminum aircraft parts, how is it treated, and what must be recorded afterward?"*
> The assistant split this into three questions and answered all three. It cited Chapter 8 (corrosion signs and treatment, pages 8-17 to 8-22) and Chapter 2 (maintenance record entries, page 2-39). That is two chapters from one question, in about 18 seconds.

**Why it makes life easier**
- One question instead of hunting through chapters.
- Every answer shows where it came from, so a technician or inspector can check the page.
- If the handbook does not cover something, the assistant says so instead of guessing.

**Completeness check ("Verify"):** after the quick answer, a second pass sweeps every section of the handbook and lists anything relevant that the answer left out. *It is built but not yet reliable; see "Not yet proven".*

**What a pilot would prove (the success measures):**
1. Do answers include every relevant section? We measure this against a question set your own experts write.
2. Do technicians spend less time finding answers than they do today?
3. Do your experts trust the citations when they spot-check them?

**Not yet proven (said out loud, not hidden):**
- We have **no measured accuracy or recall number yet**. The test set that would produce one has not been run.
- The completeness check returned an error on every test question today. It needs a fix before it is shown as working.
- Answer time was about 15–25 seconds per question. Your acceptable wait time is still an open question.

---

## 90-second talk track

**(0:00)** "Your technicians already have the answers. They are in the handbooks. The problem is that real questions don't live in one place. Ask how to deal with corrosion on an aluminum part, and the answer is in one chapter, the paperwork rule is in another, and a search finds only one of them."

**(0:20)** "So we built an assistant that has read the whole handbook, all 14 chapters and 633 pages. A technician types the question the way they would say it out loud."

**(0:35)** *Show the corrosion question.* "Watch what it does. It breaks the question into three parts: how to spot it, how to treat it, and what to record. It answers each part, and every statement has a number that links to a chapter, a section and a page. Here it pulled from Chapter 8 for the corrosion work and Chapter 2 for the record-keeping rule. One question, two chapters."

**(1:00)** "Two things matter for trust. First, nothing is unsourced: if a technician or an inspector doubts an answer, the page is right there. Second, if the handbook doesn't cover it, the assistant says so rather than inventing a number."

**(1:15)** "What we are not claiming: we haven't measured accuracy yet, and the 'did it miss anything' check isn't ready. What we'd like to do is a short pilot on your real documents, with questions your own experts write, and measure whether it finds everything and saves your people time."

**(1:30)** "That's the ask: agree on ten to fifteen real questions, and we'll show you the results."

---

## Q&A prep (20-minute live session)

| Likely question | Honest answer |
|---|---|
| How accurate is it? | Not measured yet. The pilot measures it against questions your experts write. |
| Will it miss things? | Possibly. The completeness check is meant to catch that, but it is not working reliably yet. Citations let a person check any answer. |
| Can it use our own manuals, not just the FAA handbook? | The approach is designed for that. This build covers the FAA handbook only; your documents would be a pilot step. |
| What if it's wrong? | Every claim carries a page reference, and it declines when the text doesn't support an answer. A person still makes the maintenance decision. |
| How long does it take? | About 15–25 seconds per question in today's runs. |
| What does it cost to set up and run? | Reading the 14-chapter handbook into the system cost about $3.31 in AI usage. Per-question cost has not been measured. |
| Who can see our data? | This case uses a public handbook. Handling of your private documents would be agreed before any pilot. |

---

## Evidence behind this page

| Claim on the slide | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| 14 chapters, 633 pages, all covered | `index/report.json` (documents 14, pages covered 633 of 633) |
| About $3.31 to read the handbook in | `index/report.json` (`llm_cost_usd` 3.3099) |
| Corrosion question: Ch 8 and Ch 2 cited, ~18 s | Live run of `rag.ask(mode="fast")`, 2026-11-01 |
| Completeness check errors | Live runs of `rag.ask(mode="verify")`, 3 of 3 returned `provider_unavailable` |
| No accuracy number | `evals/` does not exist yet; the recall run (acceptance criterion 5) has not been done |

## Before the live session
- Use a **real screenshot** of a fast-mode answer. `ui/screenshots/*.png` show the mock fixtures (the Verify one is partly cropped), so do not present them as real results.
- Run the corrosion question once beforehand so the demo is warm, and keep the local app as the fallback. There is no cloud URL to claim.
- Fix or hide the Verify toggle before the demo, or present it as "coming next".

69	class Tracer:
70	    """Collects one entry per pipeline step and streams it to an optional callback."""
71	
72	    def __init__(self, request_id, on_step=None):
73	        self.request_id, self.on_step = request_id, on_step
74	        self.steps, self.lock = [], threading.Lock()
75	
76	    def add(self, step, tool, detail, started, *, model=None, status="ok", cost=0.0):
77	        entry = {"step": step, "tool": tool, "model": model, "detail": detail,
78	                 "ms": int((time.time() - started) * 1000), "status": status, "cost_usd": round(cost, 6)}
79	        with self.lock:
80	            self.steps.append(entry)
81	        log.info("%s %-22s %-22s %5dms %s %s", self.request_id, step, tool, entry["ms"], status, detail[:160])
82	        if self.on_step:
83	            try:
84	                self.on_step(entry)
85	            except Exception:
86	                pass
87	        return entry
88	
89	    @property
90	    def cost(self):
91	        return round(sum(s["cost_usd"] for s in self.steps), 6)

127	    convo = "\n".join(f"{t.get('role', 'user')}: {_content_text(t.get('content'))[:1000]}"
128	                      for t in turns if isinstance(t, dict))
129	    topics = "\n".join(f"{t['topic_id']}\t{t['label']}" for t in store["taxonomy"]["topics"] if t["parent_id"])
130	    messages = [

132	            "You analyse questions for a search system over the FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician General "
133	            "Handbook. Rewrite follow-ups into a standalone question using the conversation. Split nested or "
134	            "multi-part questions into 1-4 self-contained sub_questions (one if the question is simple). "
135	            "topics: topic_ids from the list that the question is about (may be empty). keyword_query: exact "
136	            "terms, part numbers and regulation references for keyword search. needs_clarification: a short "
137	            "question to ask the user only if the question cannot be answered without it, else null.")},
138	        {"role": "user", "content": f"Topic list:\n{topics}\n\nConversation so far:\n{convo or '(none)'}\n\nQuestion: {question}"},
139	    ]

141	                         max_tokens=1500, timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S)

143	    out["topics"] = [t for t in out["topics"] if t in valid]
144	    out["sub_questions"] = [q for q in out["sub_questions"] if q.strip()][:4] or [out["standalone_question"] or question]

148	def search(sub_question, query_vec, keyword_query, intent_topics, store):
149	    """Hybrid search for one sub-question. Returns (candidates, provenance, stats):
150	    candidates = [(chunk_idx, rrf_score)] best first; provenance[idx] = ranks per retriever."""
151	    prov, rankings = {}, []
152	    stats = {"dense": 0, "section": 0, "bm25": 0}
153	    if query_vec is not None:
154	        dense = list(np.argsort(-(store["vectors"]["chunk"] @ query_vec))[:DENSE_CHUNKS])
155	        rankings.append(dense)
156	        for r, i in enumerate(dense):
157	            prov.setdefault(int(i), {})["dense_rank"] = r + 1
158	        top_sections = np.argsort(-(store["vectors"]["section"] @ query_vec))[:DENSE_SECTIONS]
159	        via_sections = []
160	        for sr, si in enumerate(top_sections):
161	            for cid in store["sections"][si]["chunk_ids"]:
162	                i = store["chunk_index"][cid]
163	                via_sections.append(i)
164	                prov.setdefault(i, {}).setdefault("section_rank", sr + 1)
165	        rankings.append(via_sections)
166	        stats["dense"], stats["section"] = len(dense), len(top_sections)
167	    tokens = tokenize(sub_question + " " + keyword_query)
168	    if tokens:
169	        bm25 = store["bm25"].get_scores(tokens)
170	        top = [int(i) for i in np.argsort(-bm25)[:BM25_TOP] if bm25[i] > 0]
171	        rankings.append(top)
172	        for r, i in enumerate(top):
173	            prov.setdefault(i, {})["bm25_rank"] = r + 1
174	        stats["bm25"] = len(top)
175	    scores = {}
176	    for ranking in rankings:
177	        for rank, idx in enumerate(ranking):
178	            scores[int(idx)] = scores.get(int(idx), 0.0) + 1.0 / (RRF_K + rank + 1)
179	    wanted = set(intent_topics)
180	    if wanted:
181	        for idx in scores:  # soft boost only; topics never filter
182	            scores[idx] += TOPIC_BOOST * len(wanted & set(store["chunks"][idx]["topics"]))
183	    candidates = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:CANDIDATES]
184	    for idx, s in candidates:
185	        prov[idx]["rrf_score"] = round(s, 5)
186	    return candidates, prov, stats

189	def assess_relevance(sub_question, candidates, store):
190	    """LLM relevance assessment (replaces a local cross-encoder). Returns ({chunk_idx: (score, reason)}, record)."""
191	    passages = "\n\n".join(
192	        f"[{store['chunks'][i]['chunk_id']}] {store['chunks'][i]['section_path']}\n{store['chunks'][i]['text'][:1200]}"
193	        for i, _ in candidates)
194	    messages = [
195	        {"role": "system", "content": (
196	            "Score how well each passage helps answer the question, using only the passage text. "
197	            "3 = directly answers part of it, 2 = relevant supporting detail, 1 = same topic but not useful, "
198	            "0 = unrelated. Return one score per chunk_id.")},
199	        {"role": "user", "content": f"Question: {sub_question}\n\nPassages:\n{passages}"},
200	    ]
201	    out, rec = chat_json(messages, "relevance", RELEVANCE_SCHEMA, prompt_version="relevance.v1", kind="relevance",
202	                         max_tokens=4000, timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S)
203	    by_id = {store["chunks"][i]["chunk_id"]: i for i, _ in candidates}
204	    return {by_id[s["chunk_id"]]: (s["score"], s["reason"]) for s in out["scores"] if s["chunk_id"] in by_id}, rec

207	def expand_context(selected, store):
208	    """For each selected chunk, add its section neighbours (or the whole section if small), within budget."""
209	    budget = CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS
210	    contexts = {}
211	    for idx in selected:
212	        chunk = store["chunks"][idx]
213	        section = store["sections"][store["section_index"][chunk["section_id"]]]
214	        sec_idxs = [store["chunk_index"][c] for c in section["chunk_ids"]]
215	        if sum(store["chunks"][i]["token_count"] for i in sec_idxs) <= SMALL_SECTION_TOKENS:
216	            window = sec_idxs
217	        else:
218	            pos = sec_idxs.index(idx)
219	            window = sec_idxs[max(0, pos - 1):pos + 2]
220	        cost = sum(store["chunks"][i]["token_count"] for i in window)
221	        if cost > budget:
222	            window, cost = [idx], chunk["token_count"]
223	        if cost > budget:
224	            break
225	        budget -= cost
226	        contexts[idx] = "\n\n".join(store["chunks"][i]["text"] for i in window)
227	    return contexts, CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS - budget

260	def ask(question, history=None, mode="fast", *, on_step=None):
261	    started = time.time()
262	    mode = mode if mode in ("fast", "verify") else "fast"
263	    tracer = Tracer(uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], on_step)
264	
265	    def finish(**fields):
266	        result = {"answer_markdown": "", "citations": [], "intent": None, "sub_questions": [], "coverage": None,
267	                  "insufficient_evidence": False, "mode": mode, "latency_ms": 0, "error": None,
268	                  "request_id": tracer.request_id, "trace": tracer.steps, "cost_usd": 0.0}
269	        result.update(fields)
270	        result["latency_ms"] = int((time.time() - started) * 1000)
271	        result["cost_usd"] = tracer.cost
272	        tracer.add("done", "rag.ask", f"{result['latency_ms']} ms total, ${result['cost_usd']:.4f}, "
273	                   f"{len(result['citations'])} citations", started,
274	                   status="error" if result["error"] else "ok")
275	        _write_log(result, question)
276	        return result
277	
278	    t = time.time()
279	    if not question or not question.strip():
280	        tracer.add("validate", "rag.ask", "empty question", t, status="error")
281	        return finish(error={"code": "empty_question", "message": "Please enter a question."})
282	    if len(question) > MAX_QUESTION_CHARS:
283	        tracer.add("validate", "rag.ask", f"{len(question)} chars > {MAX_QUESTION_CHARS}", t, status="error")
284	        return finish(error={"code": "question_too_long", "message": f"Questions are limited to {MAX_QUESTION_CHARS} characters."})
285	    try:
286	        store = get_store()
287	    except (StoreError, OSError) as e:
288	        tracer.add("load_index", "pickle", str(e), t, status="error")
289	        return finish(error={"code": "index_missing", "message": str(e)})
290	    tracer.add("load_index", "pickle (in memory)",
291	               f"{len(store['chunks'])} chunks, {len(store['sections'])} sections, {len(store['documents'])} chapters", t)
292	
293	    error = None
294	    t = time.time()
295	    try:
296	        intent, rec = classify_intent(question, history, store)
297	        tracer.add("intent", "openrouter.chat", f"{intent['primary']}; {len(intent['sub_questions'])} sub-questions; "
298	                   f"topics {intent['topics'][:4]}", t, model=rec["model"], cost=_cost(rec))
299	    except ProviderError as e:
300	        error = {"code": "provider_unavailable", "message": f"Intent step unavailable: {e}"}
301	        intent = {"standalone_question": question, "primary": "multi_hop", "intents": [], "topics": [],
302	                  "entities": [], "sub_questions": [question], "keyword_query": "", "needs_clarification": None}
303	        tracer.add("intent", "openrouter.chat", str(e), t, model=model_name("LLM_MODEL"), status="error")
304	    sub_questions = intent["sub_questions"]
305	
306	    t = time.time()
307	    try:
308	        query_vecs = embed(sub_questions, model=model_name("EMBEDDING_MODEL"), timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S)
309	        tracer.add("embed_query", "openrouter.embeddings", f"{len(sub_questions)} vectors x 1536", t,
310	                   model=model_name("EMBEDDING_MODEL"))
311	    except ProviderError as e:
312	        error = error or {"code": "provider_unavailable", "message": f"Embeddings unavailable, keyword search only: {e}"}
313	        query_vecs = [None] * len(sub_questions)
314	        tracer.add("embed_query", "openrouter.embeddings", f"failed, BM25 only: {e}", t,
315	                   model=model_name("EMBEDDING_MODEL"), status="error")
316	
317	    results = []
318	    for qi, (q, v) in enumerate(zip(sub_questions, query_vecs)):
319	        t = time.time()
320	        candidates, prov, stats = search(q, v, intent["keyword_query"], intent["topics"], store)
321	        results.append((candidates, prov))
322	        tracer.add(f"search[{qi + 1}]", "numpy.dense + rank_bm25 + rrf",
323	                   f"dense {stats['dense']} chunks, {stats['section']} sections, BM25 {stats['bm25']} -> "
324	                   f"RRF top {len(candidates)} for '{q[:60]}'", t)
325	
326	    def assess(args):
327	        qi, q, candidates = args
328	        t0 = time.time()
329	        try:
330	            scored, rec = assess_relevance(q, candidates, store)
331	            kept = sum(1 for s, _ in scored.values() if s >= 2)
332	            tracer.add(f"relevance[{qi + 1}]", "openrouter.chat", f"scored {len(scored)}, kept {kept} (score>=2)",
333	                       t0, model=rec["model"], cost=_cost(rec))
334	            return scored
335	        except ProviderError as e:
336	            tracer.add(f"relevance[{qi + 1}]", "openrouter.chat", f"failed, using RRF order: {e}", t0,
337	                       model=model_name("LLM_MODEL"), status="error")
338	            return None
339	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
340	        assessments = list(pool.map(assess, [(qi, q, r[0]) for qi, (q, r) in enumerate(zip(sub_questions, results))]))
341	
342	    # Keep relevant chunks per sub-question, best first; remember provenance for each.
343	    selected, relevance, retrieval = [], {}, {}
344	    for qi, ((candidates, prov), scored) in enumerate(zip(results, assessments)):
345	        if scored is None:
346	            error = error or {"code": "provider_unavailable", "message": "Relevance assessment unavailable; using fused ranking."}
347	            keep = [(i, 2, "relevance step unavailable; kept by RRF rank") for i, _ in candidates[:KEEP_PER_SUBQ]]
348	        else:
349	            ranked = sorted(((i, scored[i][0], s, scored[i][1]) for i, s in candidates if i in scored and scored[i][0] >= 2),
350	                            key=lambda r: (-r[1], -r[2]))
351	            keep = [(i, sc, reason) for i, sc, _, reason in ranked[:KEEP_PER_SUBQ]]
352	        for i, sc, reason in keep:
353	            if sc > relevance.get(i, -1):
354	                relevance[i] = sc
355	                retrieval[i] = {"sub_question": sub_questions[qi], "dense_rank": prov[i].get("dense_rank"),
356	                                "section_rank": prov[i].get("section_rank"), "bm25_rank": prov[i].get("bm25_rank"),
357	                                "rrf_score": prov[i].get("rrf_score"), "relevance_reason": reason}
358	            if i not in selected:
359	                selected.append(i)
360	
361	    if time.time() - started > FAST_TIMEOUT_S:
362	        return finish(intent=_public_intent(intent),
363	                      error={"code": "timeout", "message": "Search took too long; please try a narrower question."})
364	
365	    t = time.time()
366	    contexts, used_tokens = expand_context(selected, store)
367	    tracer.add("context", "rag.expand_context", f"{len(contexts)} passages, ~{used_tokens} of {CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS} tokens", t)
368	    numbered = list(contexts)
369	    citations = [_citation(n + 1, idx, store, relevance[idx], retrieval[idx], contexts[idx]) for n, idx in enumerate(numbered)]
370	    insufficient = not numbered
371	    answer_md = ""
372	    sub_out = [{"question": q, "citation_ns": [c["n"] for c in citations if c["retrieval"]["sub_question"] == q]}
373	               for q in sub_questions]
374	
375	    if numbered:
376	        passages = "\n\n".join(f"[{c['n']}] {c['section_path']} (page {c['page_label']})\n{c['passage']}" for c in citations)
377	        messages = [
378	            {"role": "system", "content": (
379	                "You answer questions for aircraft maintenance staff using only the numbered passages from the FAA "
380	                "Aviation Maintenance Technician General Handbook. Cover every part of the question. Put a [n] "
381	                "citation after every claim. Include any warnings or cautions the passages give. If the passages do "
382	                "not cover a part of the question, say so plainly for that part. If they support no answer at all, "
383	                "set insufficient_evidence to true. Never invent values, limits, torque figures or procedures.")},
384	            {"role": "user", "content": f"Question: {intent['standalone_question'] or question}\n\nSub-questions: {sub_questions}\n\nPassages:\n{passages}"},
385	        ]
386	        t = time.time()
387	        try:
388	            out, rec = chat_json(messages, "answer", ANSWER_SCHEMA, model=model_name("ANSWER_MODEL"),
389	                                 prompt_version="answer.v1", kind="answer", max_tokens=3000, timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S)
390	            answer_md, insufficient = out["answer_markdown"], out["insufficient_evidence"]
391	            valid_ns = {c["n"] for c in citations}
392	            sub_out = [{"question": s["question"], "citation_ns": [n for n in s["citation_ns"] if n in valid_ns]}
393	                       for s in out["sub_answers"]] or sub_out
394	            used = {int(n) for n in re.findall(r"\[(\d+)\]", answer_md)}
395	            if used:
396	                citations = [c for c in citations if c["n"] in used]
397	            tracer.add("answer", "openrouter.chat", f"{len(answer_md)} chars, cites {sorted(used)}; "
398	                       f"insufficient_evidence={insufficient}", t, model=rec["model"], cost=_cost(rec))
399	        except ProviderError as e:
400	            error = {"code": "provider_unavailable", "message": f"Answer model unavailable; showing the best passages: {e}"}
401	            answer_md = "\n\n".join(f"[{c['n']}] {c['section_path']} (p. {c['page_label']}): {c['snippet']}" for c in citations)
402	            tracer.add("answer", "openrouter.chat", str(e), t, model=model_name("ANSWER_MODEL"), status="error")
403	    else:
404	        answer_md = "The handbook passages found do not support an answer to this question."
405	        tracer.add("answer", "openrouter.chat", "skipped: no relevant passages", time.time(),
406	                   model=model_name("ANSWER_MODEL"), status="skipped")
407	
408	    coverage = None
409	    if mode == "verify":
410	        t = time.time()
411	        try:
412	            from rag.verify import verify_coverage
413	            coverage = verify_coverage(question, _public_intent(intent), citations, store)
414	            for m in coverage.get("missed_sections", []):
415	                sec = store["sections"][store["section_index"][m["section_id"]]]

423	        except TimeoutError as e:

425	            tracer.add("verify", "rag.verify", str(e), t, status="error")
426	        except Exception as e:  # never raise to the UI
427	            error = error or {"code": "provider_unavailable", "message": f"Verify sweep unavailable: {e}"}
428	            tracer.add("verify", "rag.verify", str(e), t, status="error")
429	
430	    return finish(answer_markdown=answer_md, citations=citations, intent=_public_intent(intent),
431	                  sub_questions=sub_out, coverage=coverage, insufficient_evidence=insufficient, error=error)

57	        self._dirty = 0
58	        self.data = {}
59	        if self.path.exists():
60	            with open(self.path, "rb") as f:
61	                self.data = pickle.load(f)  # only files written by this pipeline
62	
63	    def get(self, key):
64	        with self.lock:
65	            return self.data.get(key)
66	
67	    def put(self, key, value):
68	        with self.lock:
69	            self.data[key] = value
70	            self._dirty += 1
71	            if self._dirty >= self.autosave_every:
72	                self._save()
73	
74	    def save(self):
75	        with self.lock:
76	            self._save()
77	
78	    def _save(self):
79	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
80	        tmp = self.path.with_suffix(".tmp")
81	        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
82	            pickle.dump(self.data, f, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
83	        os.replace(tmp, self.path)

87	def _post(path, body, timeout):
88	    key = os.environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")
89	    if not key:
90	        raise ProviderError("OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set")
91	    request = urllib.request.Request(
92	        f"{BASE_URL}{path}",
93	        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
94	        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
95	        method="POST",
96	    )
97	    last = None
98	    for attempt in range(3):
99	        try:
100	            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
101	                result = json.load(response)
102	            if "error" in result:
103	                raise ProviderError(f"{path}: {str(result['error'])[:300]}")
104	            return result
105	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
106	            last = ProviderError(f"{path}: HTTP {e.code} {e.read().decode(errors='replace')[:300]}")
107	            if e.code not in RETRYABLE:
108	                raise last
109	        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, ProviderError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
110	            last = e if isinstance(e, ProviderError) else ProviderError(f"{path}: {e}")
111	        time.sleep(2 * 2 ** attempt)
112	    raise last

115	def _hash(obj):
116	    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode()).hexdigest()
117

119	def chat_json(messages, schema_name, schema, *, model=None, prompt_version, kind,
120	              cache=None, max_tokens=4000, timeout=120):
121	    """Run a strict json_schema chat completion. Returns (parsed_json, record)."""
122	    model = model or model_name("LLM_MODEL")
123	    key = _hash({"model": model, "prompt_version": prompt_version, "messages": messages, "schema": schema})
124	    if cache is not None:
125	        hit = cache.get(key)
126	        if hit is not None:
127	            return hit["response_json"], {**hit, "request_sha256": key, "cached": True}
128	    result = _post("/chat/completions", {
129	        "model": model,
130	        "messages": messages,
131	        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
132	        "temperature": 0,
133	        "response_format": {"type": "json_schema",
134	                            "json_schema": {"name": schema_name, "strict": True, "schema": schema}},
135	        "provider": {"require_parameters": True},
136	        "usage": {"include": True},
137	    }, timeout)
138	    choice = result["choices"][0]
139	    if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length":
140	        raise ProviderError(f"{kind}: output hit max_tokens={max_tokens}")
141	    try:
142	        parsed = json.loads(choice["message"]["content"])
143	    except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
144	        raise ProviderError(f"{kind}: invalid JSON from model: {e}")
145	    record = {"model": result.get("model", model), "prompt_version": prompt_version, "request_kind": kind,
146	              "response_json": parsed, "usage": result.get("usage", {}),
147	              "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}
148	    if cache is not None:
149	        cache.put(key, record)
150	    return parsed, {**record, "request_sha256": key, "cached": False}
151	
152	
153	def embed(texts, *, model=None, cache=None, batch_size=128, timeout=60):
154	    """Embed texts; returns an L2-normalized float32 array of shape (len(texts), 1536)."""
155	    model = model or model_name("EMBEDDING_MODEL")
156	    keys = [hashlib.sha256(f"{model}\n{t}".encode()).hexdigest() for t in texts]
157	    vectors = {}
158	    missing = []
159	    for k, t in zip(keys, texts):
160	        hit = cache.get(k) if cache is not None else None
161	        if hit is not None:
162	            vectors[k] = hit
163	        elif k not in vectors:
164	            missing.append((k, t))
165	            vectors[k] = None
166	    for i in range(0, len(missing), batch_size):
167	        batch = missing[i:i + batch_size]
168	        result = _post("/embeddings", {"model": model, "input": [t for _, t in batch]}, timeout)
169	        for item in sorted(result["data"], key=lambda d: d["index"]):
170	            k = batch[item["index"]][0]
171	            v = np.asarray(item["embedding"], dtype=np.float32)
172	            if v.shape != (EMBEDDING_DIMS,):
173	                raise ProviderError(f"embedding has shape {v.shape}, expected ({EMBEDDING_DIMS},)")
174	            vectors[k] = v
175	            if cache is not None:
176	                cache.put(k, v)
177	    matrix = np.stack([vectors[k] for k in keys]) if keys else np.zeros((0, EMBEDDING_DIMS), np.float32)
178	    norms = np.linalg.norm(matrix, axis=1, keepdims=True)
179	    return (matrix / np.where(norms == 0, 1, norms)).astype(np.float32)

# CHANGE REQUEST 001 — Traceability (contract v1.1, backward-compatible)

- **Requested by:** the user, 2026-11-01. They asked for clickable source links, direct source mapping, and logs in the site that show which tools ran.
- **Approved by:** the user's request in the conversation (above).
- **Type:** backward-compatible additions to MASTER_SPEC contract B. Existing fields keep their names, types and meaning. Consumers of v1 keep working.

## Changes
1. **`ask()` takes an optional keyword `on_step: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None`.**
   - It is called once per pipeline step as the step finishes, so the UI can stream a live log.
   - Exceptions raised by the callback are ignored.
2. **The `Answer` gains these fields:**
   - `request_id: str`
   - `trace: list[Step]`, where a Step is `{step, tool, model, detail, ms, status: "ok"|"error"|"skipped", cost_usd}`. The tool is the component that ran: `openrouter.chat`, `openrouter.embeddings`, `numpy.dense`, `rank_bm25`, `rrf`, `rag.verify`, and so on.
   - `cost_usd: float`, the sum of OpenRouter-reported costs for this request.
3. **Each citation gains:**
   - `chunk_id`
   - `pdf_page`: the page in the full handbook PDF
   - `source: {pdf_file, pdf_file_page}`, for display links only
   - `retrieval: {sub_question, dense_rank, section_rank, bm25_rank, rrf_score, relevance_reason}`
   - `passage`: the exact text sent to the answer model
4. **Each `coverage.missed_sections` item gains** `source: {pdf_file, pdf_file_page}`.
5. **Backend log:** every request is appended as one JSON line to `logs/queries.jsonl` (gitignored), and each step is logged to the console.

## Corpus rule check
- The chapter PDFs in `DATA/chapters/` are used **only as display links** for citations, with the page computed from the citation's page label.
- They are never read for routing, embeddings, metadata or evaluation. MASTER_SPEC's prohibited-inputs rule is unchanged.

## Ownership
- Claude makes the UI part of this change in `ui/` on `main`, because the Cursor workstream has merged and is idle.
- Cursor must merge `main` before making any further edits to `ui/`.

1	"""rag.ask: intent -> per-sub-question hybrid search (dense + BM25 + RRF) -> LLM relevance
2	assessment -> context expansion -> grounded answer with citations (MASTER_SPEC contract B,
3	plus the v1.1 traceability fields in docs/decisions/CHANGE_REQUEST.md).

7	import logging

13	from datetime import datetime, timezone

22	           "regulatory", "navigation", "multi_hop", "out_of_scope"]

69	class Tracer:
70	    """Collects one entry per pipeline step and streams it to an optional callback."""
71	
72	    def __init__(self, request_id, on_step=None):
73	        self.request_id, self.on_step = request_id, on_step
74	        self.steps, self.lock = [], threading.Lock()

76	    def add(self, step, tool, detail, started, *, model=None, status="ok", cost=0.0):
77	        entry = {"step": step, "tool": tool, "model": model, "detail": detail,
78	                 "ms": int((time.time() - started) * 1000), "status": status, "cost_usd": round(cost, 6)}
79	        with self.lock:

82	        if self.on_step:

91	        return round(sum(s["cost_usd"] for s in self.steps), 6)

125	def classify_intent(question, history, store):
126	    turns = (history or [])[-HISTORY_TURNS:]
127	    convo = "\n".join(f"{t.get('role', 'user')}: {_content_text(t.get('content'))[:1000]}"
128	                      for t in turns if isinstance(t, dict))
129	    topics = "\n".join(f"{t['topic_id']}\t{t['label']}" for t in store["taxonomy"]["topics"] if t["parent_id"])
130	    messages = [
131	        {"role": "system", "content": (
132	            "You analyse questions for a search system over the FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician General "
133	            "Handbook. Rewrite follow-ups into a standalone question using the conversation. Split nested or "
134	            "multi-part questions into 1-4 self-contained sub_questions (one if the question is simple). "
135	            "topics: topic_ids from the list that the question is about (may be empty). keyword_query: exact "
136	            "terms, part numbers and regulation references for keyword search. needs_clarification: a short "
137	            "question to ask the user only if the question cannot be answered without it, else null.")},
138	        {"role": "user", "content": f"Topic list:\n{topics}\n\nConversation so far:\n{convo or '(none)'}\n\nQuestion: {question}"},
139	    ]
140	    out, rec = chat_json(messages, "intent", INTENT_SCHEMA, prompt_version="intent.v1", kind="intent",
141	                         max_tokens=1500, timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S)
142	    valid = {t["topic_id"] for t in store["taxonomy"]["topics"]}

144	    out["sub_questions"] = [q for q in out["sub_questions"] if q.strip()][:4] or [out["standalone_question"] or question]

148	def search(sub_question, query_vec, keyword_query, intent_topics, store):
149	    """Hybrid search for one sub-question. Returns (candidates, provenance, stats):
150	    candidates = [(chunk_idx, rrf_score)] best first; provenance[idx] = ranks per retriever."""
151	    prov, rankings = {}, []
152	    stats = {"dense": 0, "section": 0, "bm25": 0}
153	    if query_vec is not None:
154	        dense = list(np.argsort(-(store["vectors"]["chunk"] @ query_vec))[:DENSE_CHUNKS])
155	        rankings.append(dense)
156	        for r, i in enumerate(dense):
157	            prov.setdefault(int(i), {})["dense_rank"] = r + 1
158	        top_sections = np.argsort(-(store["vectors"]["section"] @ query_vec))[:DENSE_SECTIONS]
159	        via_sections = []
160	        for sr, si in enumerate(top_sections):
161	            for cid in store["sections"][si]["chunk_ids"]:
162	                i = store["chunk_index"][cid]
163	                via_sections.append(i)
164	                prov.setdefault(i, {}).setdefault("section_rank", sr + 1)
165	        rankings.append(via_sections)
166	        stats["dense"], stats["section"] = len(dense), len(top_sections)
167	    tokens = tokenize(sub_question + " " + keyword_query)
168	    if tokens:
169	        bm25 = store["bm25"].get_scores(tokens)
170	        top = [int(i) for i in np.argsort(-bm25)[:BM25_TOP] if bm25[i] > 0]
171	        rankings.append(top)
172	        for r, i in enumerate(top):
173	            prov.setdefault(i, {})["bm25_rank"] = r + 1
174	        stats["bm25"] = len(top)
175	    scores = {}
176	    for ranking in rankings:
177	        for rank, idx in enumerate(ranking):
178	            scores[int(idx)] = scores.get(int(idx), 0.0) + 1.0 / (RRF_K + rank + 1)
179	    wanted = set(intent_topics)
180	    if wanted:
181	        for idx in scores:  # soft boost only; topics never filter
182	            scores[idx] += TOPIC_BOOST * len(wanted & set(store["chunks"][idx]["topics"]))
183	    candidates = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:CANDIDATES]
184	    for idx, s in candidates:
185	        prov[idx]["rrf_score"] = round(s, 5)
186	    return candidates, prov, stats

189	def assess_relevance(sub_question, candidates, store):
190	    """LLM relevance assessment (replaces a local cross-encoder). Returns ({chunk_idx: (score, reason)}, record)."""
191	    passages = "\n\n".join(
192	        f"[{store['chunks'][i]['chunk_id']}] {store['chunks'][i]['section_path']}\n{store['chunks'][i]['text'][:1200]}"
193	        for i, _ in candidates)
194	    messages = [
195	        {"role": "system", "content": (
196	            "Score how well each passage helps answer the question, using only the passage text. "
197	            "3 = directly answers part of it, 2 = relevant supporting detail, 1 = same topic but not useful, "
198	            "0 = unrelated. Return one score per chunk_id.")},
199	        {"role": "user", "content": f"Question: {sub_question}\n\nPassages:\n{passages}"},
200	    ]
201	    out, rec = chat_json(messages, "relevance", RELEVANCE_SCHEMA, prompt_version="relevance.v1", kind="relevance",
202	                         max_tokens=4000, timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S)
203	    by_id = {store["chunks"][i]["chunk_id"]: i for i, _ in candidates}
204	    return {by_id[s["chunk_id"]]: (s["score"], s["reason"]) for s in out["scores"] if s["chunk_id"] in by_id}, rec
205	
206	
207	def expand_context(selected, store):
208	    """For each selected chunk, add its section neighbours (or the whole section if small), within budget."""
209	    budget = CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS
210	    contexts = {}
211	    for idx in selected:
212	        chunk = store["chunks"][idx]
213	        section = store["sections"][store["section_index"][chunk["section_id"]]]
214	        sec_idxs = [store["chunk_index"][c] for c in section["chunk_ids"]]
215	        if sum(store["chunks"][i]["token_count"] for i in sec_idxs) <= SMALL_SECTION_TOKENS:
216	            window = sec_idxs
217	        else:
218	            pos = sec_idxs.index(idx)
219	            window = sec_idxs[max(0, pos - 1):pos + 2]
220	        cost = sum(store["chunks"][i]["token_count"] for i in window)
221	        if cost > budget:
222	            window, cost = [idx], chunk["token_count"]
223	        if cost > budget:
224	            break
225	        budget -= cost

261	    started = time.time()
262	    mode = mode if mode in ("fast", "verify") else "fast"
263	    tracer = Tracer(uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], on_step)
264	
265	    def finish(**fields):
266	        result = {"answer_markdown": "", "citations": [], "intent": None, "sub_questions": [], "coverage": None,
267	                  "insufficient_evidence": False, "mode": mode, "latency_ms": 0, "error": None,
268	                  "request_id": tracer.request_id, "trace": tracer.steps, "cost_usd": 0.0}
269	        result.update(fields)
270	        result["latency_ms"] = int((time.time() - started) * 1000)
271	        result["cost_usd"] = tracer.cost

278	    t = time.time()

291	               f"{len(store['chunks'])} chunks, {len(store['sections'])} sections, {len(store['documents'])} chapters", t)
292	
293	    error = None
294	    t = time.time()
295	    try:
296	        intent, rec = classify_intent(question, history, store)
297	        tracer.add("intent", "openrouter.chat", f"{intent['primary']}; {len(intent['sub_questions'])} sub-questions; "
298	                   f"topics {intent['topics'][:4]}", t, model=rec["model"], cost=_cost(rec))
299	    except ProviderError as e:
300	        error = {"code": "provider_unavailable", "message": f"Intent step unavailable: {e}"}
301	        intent = {"standalone_question": question, "primary": "multi_hop", "intents": [], "topics": [],

304	    sub_questions = intent["sub_questions"]

306	    t = time.time()

313	        query_vecs = [None] * len(sub_questions)
314	        tracer.add("embed_query", "openrouter.embeddings", f"failed, BM25 only: {e}", t,
315	                   model=model_name("EMBEDDING_MODEL"), status="error")
316	
317	    results = []
318	    for qi, (q, v) in enumerate(zip(sub_questions, query_vecs)):
319	        t = time.time()

321	        results.append((candidates, prov))

324	                   f"RRF top {len(candidates)} for '{q[:60]}'", t)

326	    def assess(args):
327	        qi, q, candidates = args
328	        t0 = time.time()
329	        try:
330	            scored, rec = assess_relevance(q, candidates, store)
331	            kept = sum(1 for s, _ in scored.values() if s >= 2)
332	            tracer.add(f"relevance[{qi + 1}]", "openrouter.chat", f"scored {len(scored)}, kept {kept} (score>=2)",
333	                       t0, model=rec["model"], cost=_cost(rec))
334	            return scored
335	        except ProviderError as e:

337	                       model=model_name("LLM_MODEL"), status="error")
338	            return None
339	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:

341	
342	    # Keep relevant chunks per sub-question, best first; remember provenance for each.
343	    selected, relevance, retrieval = [], {}, {}
344	    for qi, ((candidates, prov), scored) in enumerate(zip(results, assessments)):
345	        if scored is None:

347	            keep = [(i, 2, "relevance step unavailable; kept by RRF rank") for i, _ in candidates[:KEEP_PER_SUBQ]]

350	                            key=lambda r: (-r[1], -r[2]))
351	            keep = [(i, sc, reason) for i, sc, _, reason in ranked[:KEEP_PER_SUBQ]]
352	        for i, sc, reason in keep:

361	    if time.time() - started > FAST_TIMEOUT_S:
362	        return finish(intent=_public_intent(intent),

365	    t = time.time()
366	    contexts, used_tokens = expand_context(selected, store)
367	    tracer.add("context", "rag.expand_context", f"{len(contexts)} passages, ~{used_tokens} of {CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS} tokens", t)

375	    if numbered:

377	        messages = [

382	                "not cover a part of the question, say so plainly for that part. If they support no answer at all, "
383	                "set insufficient_evidence to true. Never invent values, limits, torque figures or procedures.")},

389	                                 prompt_version="answer.v1", kind="answer", max_tokens=3000, timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S)

397	            tracer.add("answer", "openrouter.chat", f"{len(answer_md)} chars, cites {sorted(used)}; "

399	        except ProviderError as e:

401	            answer_md = "\n\n".join(f"[{c['n']}] {c['section_path']} (p. {c['page_label']}): {c['snippet']}" for c in citations)

408	    coverage = None

414	            for m in coverage.get("missed_sections", []):

1	"""OpenRouter client: structured chat completions and embeddings, with pickle caches.
2	
3	Hosted inference only. Every response is cached by request hash so a rebuild
4	replays from disk instead of paying again.
5	"""
6	import hashlib
7	import json
8	import os
9	import pickle
10	import threading
11	import time
12	import urllib.error
13	import urllib.request
14	from datetime import datetime, timezone
15	from pathlib import Path
16	
17	import numpy as np
18	
19	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
20	BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
21	DEFAULT_MODELS = {
22	    "EMBEDDING_MODEL": "openai/text-embedding-3-small",
23	    "LLM_MODEL": "openai/gpt-4.1-mini",
24	    "ANSWER_MODEL": "openai/gpt-4.1",
25	}
26	EMBEDDING_DIMS = 1536
27	RETRYABLE = {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
28	
29	
30	class ProviderError(Exception):
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	def load_env(path=ROOT / ".env"):
35	    """Load KEY=VALUE lines from .env into os.environ (existing vars win)."""
36	    if not path.exists():
37	        return
38	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
39	        line = line.strip()
40	        if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
41	            key, value = line.split("=", 1)
42	            if value.strip():
43	                os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"').strip("'"))
44	
45	
46	def model_name(var):
47	    return os.environ.get(var) or DEFAULT_MODELS[var]
48	
49	
50	class PickleCache:
51	    """A dict persisted to a pickle file, safe to use from several threads."""
52	
53	    def __init__(self, path, autosave_every=50):
54	        self.path = Path(path)
55	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
56	        self.autosave_every = autosave_every
57	        self._dirty = 0
58	        self.data = {}
59	        if self.path.exists():
60	            with open(self.path, "rb") as f:
61	                self.data = pickle.load(f)  # only files written by this pipeline
62	
63	    def get(self, key):
64	        with self.lock:
65	            return self.data.get(key)
66	
67	    def put(self, key, value):
68	        with self.lock:
69	            self.data[key] = value
70	            self._dirty += 1
71	            if self._dirty >= self.autosave_every:
72	                self._save()
73	
74	    def save(self):
75	        with self.lock:
76	            self._save()
77	
78	    def _save(self):
79	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
80	        tmp = self.path.with_suffix(".tmp")
81	        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
82	            pickle.dump(self.data, f, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
83	        os.replace(tmp, self.path)
84	        self._dirty = 0
85	
86	
87	def _post(path, body, timeout):
88	    key = os.environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")
89	    if not key:
90	        raise ProviderError("OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set")
91	    request = urllib.request.Request(
92	        f"{BASE_URL}{path}",
93	        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
94	        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
95	        method="POST",
96	    )
97	    last = None
98	    for attempt in range(3):
99	        try:
100	            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
101	                result = json.load(response)
102	            if "error" in result:
103	                raise ProviderError(f"{path}: {str(result['error'])[:300]}")
104	            return result
105	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
106	            last = ProviderError(f"{path}: HTTP {e.code} {e.read().decode(errors='replace')[:300]}")
107	            if e.code not in RETRYABLE:
108	                raise last
109	        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, ProviderError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
110	            last = e if isinstance(e, ProviderError) else ProviderError(f"{path}: {e}")
111	        time.sleep(2 * 2 ** attempt)
112	    raise last
113	
114	
115	def _hash(obj):
116	    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode()).hexdigest()
117	
118	
119	def chat_json(messages, schema_name, schema, *, model=None, prompt_version, kind,
120	              cache=None, max_tokens=4000, timeout=120):
121	    """Run a strict json_schema chat completion. Returns (parsed_json, record)."""
122	    model = model or model_name("LLM_MODEL")
123	    key = _hash({"model": model, "prompt_version": prompt_version, "messages": messages, "schema": schema})
124	    if cache is not None:
125	        hit = cache.get(key)
126	        if hit is not None:
127	            return hit["response_json"], {**hit, "request_sha256": key, "cached": True}
128	    result = _post("/chat/completions", {
129	        "model": model,
130	        "messages": messages,
131	        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
132	        "temperature": 0,
133	        "response_format": {"type": "json_schema",
134	                            "json_schema": {"name": schema_name, "strict": True, "schema": schema}},
135	        "provider": {"require_parameters": True},
136	        "usage": {"include": True},
137	    }, timeout)
138	    choice = result["choices"][0]
139	    if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length":
140	        raise ProviderError(f"{kind}: output hit max_tokens={max_tokens}")
141	    try:
142	        parsed = json.loads(choice["message"]["content"])
143	    except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
144	        raise ProviderError(f"{kind}: invalid JSON from model: {e}")
145	    record = {"model": result.get("model", model), "prompt_version": prompt_version, "request_kind": kind,
146	              "response_json": parsed, "usage": result.get("usage", {}),
147	              "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}
148	    if cache is not None:
149	        cache.put(key, record)
150	    return parsed, {**record, "request_sha256": key, "cached": False}
151	
152	
153	def embed(texts, *, model=None, cache=None, batch_size=128, timeout=60):
154	    """Embed texts; returns an L2-normalized float32 array of shape (len(texts), 1536)."""
155	    model = model or model_name("EMBEDDING_MODEL")
156	    keys = [hashlib.sha256(f"{model}\n{t}".encode()).hexdigest() for t in texts]
157	    vectors = {}
158	    missing = []
159	    for k, t in zip(keys, texts):
160	        hit = cache.get(k) if cache is not None else None
161	        if hit is not None:
162	            vectors[k] = hit
163	        elif k not in vectors:
164	            missing.append((k, t))
165	            vectors[k] = None
166	    for i in range(0, len(missing), batch_size):
167	        batch = missing[i:i + batch_size]
168	        result = _post("/embeddings", {"model": model, "input": [t for _, t in batch]}, timeout)
169	        for item in sorted(result["data"], key=lambda d: d["index"]):
170	            k = batch[item["index"]][0]
171	            v = np.asarray(item["embedding"], dtype=np.float32)
172	            if v.shape != (EMBEDDING_DIMS,):
173	                raise ProviderError(f"embedding has shape {v.shape}, expected ({EMBEDDING_DIMS},)")
174	            vectors[k] = v
175	            if cache is not None:
176	                cache.put(k, v)
177	    matrix = np.stack([vectors[k] for k in keys]) if keys else np.zeros((0, EMBEDDING_DIMS), np.float32)
178	    norms = np.linalg.norm(matrix, axis=1, keepdims=True)
179	    return (matrix / np.where(norms == 0, 1, norms)).astype(np.float32)

1	# CHANGE REQUEST 001 — Traceability (contract v1.1, backward-compatible)
2	
3	- **Requested by:** the user, 2026-11-01. They asked for clickable source links, direct source mapping, and logs in the site that show which tools ran.
4	- **Approved by:** the user's request in the conversation (above).
5	- **Type:** backward-compatible additions to MASTER_SPEC contract B. Existing fields keep their names, types and meaning. Consumers of v1 keep working.
6	
7	## Changes
8	1. **`ask()` takes an optional keyword `on_step: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None`.**
9	   - It is called once per pipeline step as the step finishes, so the UI can stream a live log.
10	   - Exceptions raised by the callback are ignored.
11	2. **The `Answer` gains these fields:**
12	   - `request_id: str`
13	   - `trace: list[Step]`, where a Step is `{step, tool, model, detail, ms, status: "ok"|"error"|"skipped", cost_usd}`. The tool is the component that ran: `openrouter.chat`, `openrouter.embeddings`, `numpy.dense`, `rank_bm25`, `rrf`, `rag.verify`, and so on.
14	   - `cost_usd: float`, the sum of OpenRouter-reported costs for this request.
15	3. **Each citation gains:**
16	   - `chunk_id`
17	   - `pdf_page`: the page in the full handbook PDF
18	   - `source: {pdf_file, pdf_file_page}`, for display links only
19	   - `retrieval: {sub_question, dense_rank, section_rank, bm25_rank, rrf_score, relevance_reason}`
20	   - `passage`: the exact text sent to the answer model
21	4. **Each `coverage.missed_sections` item gains** `source: {pdf_file, pdf_file_page}`.
22	5. **Backend log:** every request is appended as one JSON line to `logs/queries.jsonl` (gitignored), and each step is logged to the console.
23	
24	## Corpus rule check
25	- The chapter PDFs in `DATA/chapters/` are used **only as display links** for citations, with the page computed from the citation's page label.
26	- They are never read for routing, embeddings, metadata or evaluation. MASTER_SPEC's prohibited-inputs rule is unchanged.
27	
28	## Ownership
29	- Claude makes the UI part of this change in `ui/` on `main`, because the Cursor workstream has merged and is idle.
30	- Cursor must merge `main` before making any further edits to `ui/`.

description: For Claude Desktop adding document-grounded retrieval, tool calls, context or memory to an existing working AI prototype only when the client use case requires them.
---
# Retrieval, tools and memory decision workflow

Before implementing, decide if each component is **required, useful, or unnecessary**. A single LLM call may be the correct architecture.

## Retrieval
1. Confirm actual authorized documents or public data sources. Preserve source ID, title/URL, content boundaries and collection metadata.
2. Choose a model supported for embeddings (Portkey is preferred if compatible) and a simple local index for short demos. A managed vector DB needs a persistence/search requirement.
3. Define chunking, overlap, metadata, embedding configuration and version; avoid re-embedding on every question.
4. Retrieve top-k, inspect actual hits, optionally rerank, synthesize grounded answer and expose citations or 'not enough evidence'.
5. Evaluate on a small manually verified query set for relevance/Recall@k and grounding; show at least one no-answer case.

## Tools
1. Use deterministic tools for real external data or actions; prefer a typed function/API over another LLM agent.
2. Validate JSON/schema, allowlist tool actions, enforce timeouts/retry bounds and never execute arbitrary shell/user instructions from retrieved content.
3. Do not claim connected integration works until real authorized calls have succeeded. Require human authorization before writes to external services.

## Memory
1. Short-term chat history is enough for most demos; cap history length and exclude secrets. Distinguish transcript/session state from long-term memory.
2. Add database-backed persistence only for cross-session requirements; document retention and deletion behavior.

## Orchestration
Use a straightforward sequential workflow first. Pydantic AI for typed tool calls; LangGraph only for meaningful branching/checkpointing/human approval. Name each agent only if that agent has a distinct responsibility and evaluation metric.

Output: decision rationale, code limited to owned backend paths, evidence of real retrieval/tools, failure-mode tests and known limits.
